TOOLS IN THE APP (status in brackets):
- Inverters [In field testing]: Hitachi WL200, WJ200 and WJ-C1, Allen-Bradley PowerFlex 520 and 525, Danfoss FC 280 and VLT 2800 (FC 51 in the next release), Lenze 8400 over CAN, and more: Omron MX2, Mitsubishi FR-D700 and FR-E800, Schneider ATV320, Siemens V20,
- Thermocontrollers [Draft, bench only]: Read and set Omron E5CN temperature controllers over RS-485: present value, setpoint, alarms and parameters.
- OBD2 Scanner [Draft, bench only]: Car diagnostics with an ELM327 adapter (Wi-Fi or Bluetooth): trouble codes with descriptions, freeze frame, live data with CSV recording, VIN and readiness monitors, raw terminal.
- Printers [In field testing]: Check the Ethernet port and test printing on Honeywell PM45 label printers. Cable check finds a corroded plug or damaged cable by counting link drops, lost replies and slow links. Fault guide for the PM45 included.
- Setup [Draft]: Build a drive setup from the motor nameplate: choose motor, brand and drive, pick a layout (start/stop, 4-20 mA, 3 or 7 preset speeds, PID, Modbus and more) and get a backup file with the right parameters and warnings from the man
- EzSQ programs [In field testing]: Write, check, emulate and load the small programs inside Hitachi WL200 and WJ-C1 drives: step editor, ready-made programs, an on-phone emulator with inputs and outputs, read and clone from a drive.
- Bilwinco boards [In field testing]: Backup and restore of Bilwinco Q20 control boards (main program, PLC and product data) over a USB-RS232 adapter or the ServMod Box, with one folder per machine.
- Tools [In field testing]: Spirit level, magnet meter, tachometer, slow-motion study of fast machines, loupe, strobe, leak finder, ruler, picture measure, colour matcher, solar panel aiming and a sensor explorer, all from the phone's own sensors and camera.
- USB Tools [In field testing]: USB stick analyser: partitions, raw sectors, speed and surface scan, a check for sticks that claim more space than they have, format, repair and a file browser. Works even when Android does not mount the stick.
- NFC & Barcode [Draft, bench only]: Scan and program NFC tags and barcodes. A tag opens a backup, a manual or any tool in ServMod. Make QR and barcode stickers and print them.
- ICE printers (Zodiac) [Draft, bench only]: Library of ICE (Zodiac HS, Hawk) CLARiTY printer clone files sorted by machine and date, with label preview, compare and copy to a pendrive for the printer. Shown as the ICE card inside Printers in the next release.
- ServMod Box [In field testing]: Our own ESP32-S3 interface with RS-485, RS-232, CAN, USB host and Ethernet, reached over Wi-Fi or Bluetooth. Reads Danfoss FC 280 as fast as a USB adapter, and a restore keeps running inside the Box if the phone link drops. The ha
- Backup [In field testing]: Encrypted copy of the app's own data (settings, drive backups, notes, photos, tags) to a folder you choose, such as Google Drive, with restore on a new phone and an optional daily copy.
- Steppers [Draft, bench only]: Stepper motor test bench through the ServMod Box: run, jog, moves, speed and acceleration ladders, resonance sweep and endurance tests. A simulator is included.
- HMI [Draft, simulator only]: Remote operator panel for PLCs: live inputs, outputs, analog values, timers, counters, setpoints, trends and alarms. It runs on a built-in simulator for now; real protocols are added step by step.
- Siemens OP17 [In field testing, spare panels only]: Loader for Siemens OP17 operator panels: read the panel memory directly or record a ProTool / ProSave transfer, import ProSave .psr files, and write to a spare panel. Writing has worked on spare panels; experimental, for spare pan
- PLC [Draft, bench only]: Read Omron (FINS over UDP) and Allen-Bradley (EtherNet/IP) controllers with live values and a change list. It never writes to the PLC.
- Condition [In field testing]: Vibration and sound checks with history, to compare before and after service.
- Network [In field testing]: Wi-Fi, Ethernet and Bluetooth analyser, ping, port scan and Modbus TCP read.
- Calc [Ready]: Power, cable size (recommended and minimum), resistor colour code, wiring colours (UK) and Ethernet T568A/B.
- Access [Ready]: Machine passwords in an encrypted vault, unlocked with the phone's screen lock.
- Notes [Ready]: Service notes with photos and drawing on top of the photo.
- Parts [Ready]: Search the warehouse list on the phone. Import CSV or XLSX files with automatic column matching. Next release: find a part by taking a photo of it, matched on the phone (optionally with Google Gemini and your own key); not yet tri
- My Stuff [Draft, bench only]: Your manuals: PDFs you download and keep offline, opened from the phone or by an NFC tag or barcode.
- ESP32 Loader [Ready]: Flash ESP32, ESP32-S3 and CYD boards over USB from .bin files, with checksum verification. Pro users can download the ServMod Box firmware straight into the loader.
- Werma [Draft]: Read, edit and write the configuration of a Werma eSIGN signal tower over its USB-C port: colours, effects and brightness for each input combination. Signal Tower mode lights a fixed band for each input; Filling Level mode works a
- Charger [Draft]: Phone-side charging meter: power, voltage, current, battery temperature and charge phase, a graph with CSV export, battery health and wear, and a 60 second stability test to compare saved chargers and cables. It measures on the ph
- Appearance [Draft]: Optional one-handed thumb-wheel layout for the home screen, Tools, Parts and the drive lists, and a choice of interface language. Next release, not yet tried on a phone.
DEVICES AND HOW THEY CONNECT:
- Hitachi WL200 (tested on a real drive): USB cable from the phone (USB-C with OTG adapter) to the mini-USB port on the keypad. The drive is powered from the mains, so the phone only talks to  | USB-RS485 adapter on control terminals SP and SN (A/+ to SP, B/- to SN). | ServMod Box: its USB host port to the mini-USB port, or its RS-485 channel to SP and SN.
- Hitachi WJ C1 (tested on a real drive): USB-RS485 adapter on control terminals SP and SN (A/+ to SP, B/- to SN). | ServMod Box RS-485 channel to SP and SN, wireless to the phone. | ServMod Box USB host port to the micro-USB port under the keypad cover.
- Hitachi WJ200 (not yet tried on a real drive): USB cable to the mini-USB port on the keypad. | USB-RS485 adapter on control terminals SP and SN. | ServMod Box USB host or RS-485 channel.
- Allen-Bradley PowerFlex 525 (tested on a real drive): USB-RS485 adapter on the DSI port (RJ45, pins 4 and 5). This is not an Ethernet port: never plug an Ethernet cable into it. | ServMod Box RS-485 channel to the same pins.
- Danfoss VLT FC 280 (tested on a real drive): USB-B service port on the drive: USB-C to USB-B cable straight into a USB-C phone. | USB-RS485 adapter on terminals 68 (P/+) and 69 (N/-). 9600 baud, 8E1, slave 1. Swap the two wires if there is no answer. | ServMod Box RS-485 channel to 68 and 69.
- Danfoss VLT 2800 (tested on a real drive): USB-RS485 adapter on terminals 68 (P) and 69 (N). 9600 baud, 8E1, terminal 61 is the screen. | ServMod Box RS-485 channel to 68 and 69. | Or use the front DB9 connector instead of the terminals: pin 8 (P) and pin 9 (N), pin 3 = GND.
- Danfoss VLT Micro Drive FC 51 (tested on a real drive): USB-RS485 adapter on terminals 68 (P/+) and 69 (N/-). FC protocol, 9600 baud, 8E1, slave 1. Swap the two wires if there is no answer. | ServMod Box RS-485 channel to 68 and 69 (not yet tried on a drive).
- Lenze 8400 StateLine C (tested on a real drive): ServMod Box CAN channel to the X1 terminals CH, CL and CG (CAN-High, CAN-Low, ground). Twisted pair, terminated at both ends.
- Omron 3G3MX2 (MX2) (not yet tried on a real drive): USB-RS485 adapter on the control terminals: A (D+) to RS+, B (D-) to RS-. Defaults: slave 1, 9600 baud, 8-N-1. Switch on the 120 ohm termination on th | ServMod Box RS-485 channel to RS+ and RS-.
- Mitsubishi FR-D700 (not yet tried on a real drive): USB-RS485 adapter on the PU connector (RJ45): the signal pair is made by joining pins 3 and 5 and pins 4 and 6. Do not use the power pins. | ServMod Box RS-485 channel to the same pins.
- Schneider ATV320 (not yet tried on a real drive): USB-RS485 adapter on the Modbus RJ45 port: D1 on pin 4 and D0 on pin 5. Do not connect pin 7 (10 V supply). | ServMod Box RS-485 channel to the same pins.
- Siemens SINAMICS V20 (not yet tried on a real drive): USB-RS485 adapter on terminals 6 (P+) and 7 (N-). | ServMod Box RS-485 channel to terminals 6 and 7.
- Delta MS300 (not yet tried on a real drive): USB-RS485 adapter on the RJ45 port: SG+ on pin 5 and SG- on pin 4. Do not connect pin 8 (+10 V). | ServMod Box RS-485 channel to the same pins.
- INVT GD200A (not yet tried on a real drive): USB-RS485 adapter on terminals 485+ and 485-. | ServMod Box RS-485 channel to the same terminals.
- ABB ACS355 (not yet tried on a real drive): USB-RS485 adapter on connector X1 of the FMBA-01 Modbus adapter module (adapter A+ to X1.2, B- to X1.3, ground to X1.4). | ServMod Box RS-485 channel to the same terminals.
- Inovance MD500 (not yet tried on a real drive): USB-RS485 adapter on terminals 485+ and 485-. | ServMod Box RS-485 channel to the same terminals.
- Yaskawa GA500 (not yet tried on a real drive): USB-RS485 adapter on terminals D+ and D- of TB4. Switch S2 to ON on the last drive. | ServMod Box RS-485 channel to D+ and D-.
- Omron E5CN temperature controller (not yet tried on a real drive): USB-RS485 adapter on terminals 11 (B+) and 12 (A-). The model needs the communications option; 120 ohm termination at both ends of the line. | ServMod Box RS-485 channel to terminals 11 and 12.
- Siemens OP17 operator panel (draft): USB-RS232 adapter (FTDI) to the DB15 IF1A port of the panel. | ServMod Box with the USB-RS232 adapter plugged into its USB host port, wireless to the phone.
FAQ:
Q: Do I need internet to use ServMod? A: No. Drive work, backups, wiring and fault codes all work offline. The app goes online only when you choose it: Check for updates, the optional cloud Backup folder, or Nameplate (Read with AI).
Q: Which phone do I need? A: An Android 7.0 or newer phone or tablet with USB host (OTG). Most phones from the last several years have it.
Q: Which cable or adapter do I need? A: For drives, a USB-RS485 adapter with an FTDI, CP210x, CH34x or CH343 chip. For printers, a USB-C Ethernet adapter. See the connection guides.
Q: Can it damage my equipment? A: Writing parameters or running a motor can make machinery move or stop unexpectedly. Back up first, check every written value and test on the bench before a production machine. Read the terms of use.
Q: Does it work on iPhone? A: No. ServMod is Android only.
Q: Will it support my drive or PLC? A: More models are planned. Tell us what you need through the support form. Tell us the exact model and the protocol, if you know it.
Q: What if I lose my phone? A: Each licence will be tied to your account email. Sign in, enter the Device ID of the new phone and get a new activation code.

fc280.name: Live zero error
fc280.meaning: The signal on analog input 53 or 54 has fallen below 50% of the low end configured for that input (par. 6-10, 6-20 or 6-22).
checks: Check wiring and connectors on terminals 53/54 and the signal source
Compare the live signal with the low-voltage/low-current scaling in 6-10, 6-20, 6-22
Review live-zero timeout settings 6-00 and 6-01

fc280.name: No motor
fc280.meaning: No motor is detected on the drive output.
checks: Check that the motor cable is connected at both the drive and the motor
Check for an open motor circuit or contactor in the output

fc280.name: Mains phase loss
fc280.meaning: A supply phase is missing or the supply voltage imbalance is too high. Mains distortion can also cause it.
checks: Measure all three supply phases and the voltage balance at the drive input
Check input fuses, contactor and supply cables
Consider a line filter if the supply is distorted
See par. 14-12 for the imbalance reaction

fc280.name: DC overvoltage
fc280.meaning: The DC-link voltage has exceeded its limit. Mains distortion can also cause it.
checks: Lengthen the deceleration ramp or enable over-voltage control (2-17)
Check for an overhauling load or regenerative energy; add brake resistor if needed
Check supply voltage level and quality; consider a line filter

fc280.name: DC undervoltage
fc280.meaning: The DC-link voltage has dropped below the low-voltage warning limit. Mains distortion can also cause it.
checks: Measure the supply voltage and check for sags or dips
Check input fuses and contactors for voltage drop under load
Consider a line filter if the supply is distorted

fc280.name: Inverter overloaded
fc280.meaning: The drive has been carrying more than 100% load for too long.
checks: Compare motor current (16-14) and inverter thermal (16-35) with the rating
Reduce the load or use a larger drive
Check ramp times and the switching frequency setting (14-01)

fc280.name: Motor ETR overtemperature
fc280.meaning: The electronic thermal model says the motor is too hot after running above 100% load too long.
checks: Check actual motor load and cooling
Verify motor nameplate current in 1-24 and the thermal protection setting in 1-90
Look at motor thermal readout 16-18

fc280.name: Motor thermistor overtemperature
fc280.meaning: The thermistor or its wiring is disconnected, or the motor is overheated.
checks: Check the thermistor wiring and connection to the selected input (1-93)
Check motor cooling and load
Verify the digital input mode (5-00) matches the thermistor wiring

fc280.name: Torque limit
fc280.meaning: Torque has exceeded the motor-mode limit (4-16) or generator-mode limit (4-17).
checks: Check load and mechanical binding
Review the limits in 4-16 and 4-17
Lengthen the ramp times if the limit is hit during acceleration or deceleration

fc280.name: Overcurrent
fc280.meaning: The inverter peak current limit was exceeded. If it appears at power-up, power cables may be wired to the motor terminals by mistake.
checks: Check that the supply cables are not connected to the motor terminals
Check motor and cable insulation and that the motor data matches the nameplate (1-2*)
Lengthen the acceleration ramp or reduce the load
Check for a locked or jammed mechanism

fc280.name: Ground fault
fc280.meaning: Current is leaking from the output phases to ground.
checks: Disconnect the motor and megger the cable and motor to earth
Check for damp or damaged motor cable and motor winding insulation
Check any output filter or long cable runs

fc280.name: Short circuit
fc280.meaning: There is a short circuit in the motor or at the motor terminals.
checks: Disconnect the motor and test phase-to-phase resistance of the cable and winding
Check the motor terminal box and connections for damage

fc280.name: Control word timeout
fc280.meaning: The drive is no longer receiving communication from the master.
checks: Check the fieldbus or serial cable and the master's status
Review timeout time and function (8-03 and 8-04)
Verify the protocol, address and baud rate settings (8-3*)

fc280.name: Brake resistor short-circuited
fc280.meaning: The brake resistor is shorted, so the brake function has been disabled.
checks: Disconnect and measure the brake resistor and its cable
Check the resistor value against 2-11

fc280.name: Brake overload
fc280.meaning: Power sent to the brake resistor over the last 120 s exceeded the allowed limit.
checks: Reduce regenerative energy with a lower speed or longer deceleration ramp
Check brake resistor ratings (2-11, 2-12)
Check the braking duty cycle

fc280.name: Brake IGBT/chopper short-circuited
fc280.meaning: The brake transistor is shorted, so the brake function has been disabled.
checks: Remove the brake resistor and power-cycle to test
If the alarm persists the drive needs service; contact the supplier

fc280.name: Brake check
fc280.meaning: The brake resistor is not connected or not working.
checks: Check brake resistor wiring and continuity
Check the resistor value in 2-11

fc280.name: Motor phase U missing
fc280.meaning: Motor output phase U is not present.
checks: Check the U wiring, terminals and any output contactor or filter
Measure winding resistance between phases

fc280.name: Motor phase V missing
fc280.meaning: Motor output phase V is not present.
checks: Check the V wiring, terminals and any output contactor or filter
Measure winding resistance between phases

fc280.name: Motor phase W missing
fc280.meaning: Motor output phase W is not present.
checks: Check the W wiring, terminals and any output contactor or filter
Measure winding resistance between phases

fc280.name: Fieldbus fault
fc280.meaning: PROFIBUS communication problems have occurred.
checks: Check the bus cable, terminations and connectors
Check master configuration and address
Check for EMC interference on the bus

fc280.name: Option fault
fc280.meaning: The fieldbus option reports internal faults.
checks: Power-cycle the drive
Check that the option card is seated correctly
Contact the supplier if it repeats

fc280.name: Mains failure
fc280.meaning: Active only when the supply voltage is below the level in 14-11 and 14-10 is not set to No function.
checks: Check the supply voltage and for dips or outages
Review 14-10 and 14-11

fc280.name: Internal fault
fc280.meaning: An internal drive fault has occurred.
checks: Note the fault reason in 15-31
Power-cycle the drive
Contact the local Danfoss supplier

fc280.name: Overload on terminal 27
fc280.meaning: The digital output on terminal 27 is overloaded.
checks: Check the load connected to terminal 27
Remove any short circuit on the terminal

fc280.name: Gate drive voltage fault
fc280.meaning: A fault in the gate-drive supply of the power card has been detected.
checks: Power-cycle the drive
Check for control-terminal shorts that overload internal supplies
Contact the supplier if it repeats

fc280.name: 24 V supply low
fc280.meaning: The 24 V DC supply may be overloaded.
checks: Check the load on the control terminals (24 V outputs)
Look for shorts or overloaded options

fc280.name: Speed limit
fc280.meaning: Motor speed is below the trip speed low limit set in 1-87.
checks: Check the load and settings in 1-87
Check for mechanical binding or a stalled motor

fc280.name: AMA calibration failed
fc280.meaning: A calibration error occurred during the automatic motor adaptation.
checks: Check motor data entered in 1-2* against the nameplate
Check motor cable and connections, then repeat AMA on a cold motor

fc280.name: AMA check Unom and Inom
fc280.meaning: The motor voltage and/or motor current settings are wrong.
checks: Re-enter voltage and current from the motor nameplate (1-22, 1-24)

fc280.name: AMA low Inom
fc280.meaning: The motor current is too low for AMA.
checks: Check the motor current setting (1-24) and the motor connection

fc280.name: AMA big motor
fc280.meaning: The motor is too large for AMA to run.
checks: Check that the drive is rated suitably for the motor
Enter the motor data manually

fc280.name: AMA small motor
fc280.meaning: The motor is too small for AMA to run.
checks: Check that the motor size matches the drive
Enter the motor data manually

fc280.name: AMA parameter range
fc280.meaning: Motor parameter values are outside the acceptable range, so AMA does not run.
checks: Recheck the nameplate data entered in 1-2*

fc280.name: AMA interrupt
fc280.meaning: The AMA was interrupted.
checks: Do not press stop or remove the run signal during AMA
Repeat the AMA

fc280.name: AMA timeout
fc280.meaning: The AMA timed out.
checks: Repeat AMA and check motor data and connection

fc280.name: AMA internal
fc280.meaning: An internal fault occurred during AMA.
checks: Contact Danfoss or the supplier

fc280.name: Current limit
fc280.meaning: The drive is overloaded and has reached its current limit.
checks: Reduce the load or lengthen the acceleration ramp
Check current limit setting 4-18
Check for jammed mechanics

fc280.name: External interlock
fc280.meaning: The external interlock input has been activated.
checks: Check the circuit wired to the digital input programmed as external interlock
Clear the cause, then reset

fc280.name: Encoder loss
fc280.meaning: The encoder or feedback signal was lost.
checks: Check encoder wiring, supply and settings in 4-3*

fc280.name: Mechanical brake low
fc280.meaning: The motor current did not reach the brake release current within the start delay.
checks: Check the release brake current setting (2-20) and the start delay
Check the motor connection and that the current can build up

fc280.name: Control card temperature
fc280.meaning: The control card cut-out temperature has exceeded its upper limit.
checks: Check the ambient temperature and cabinet ventilation
Check fans and filters; clean heatsink airways
Read the control card temperature in 16-39

fc280.name: Option change
fc280.meaning: A new option has been detected or a fitted one removed.
checks: Confirm the option change is intended, then reset
Check the option card seating

fc280.name: Safe Torque Off
fc280.meaning: STO has been activated. In manual restart mode, restore 24 V DC to terminals 37 and 38 and give a reset; in automatic restart mode, applying 24 V resumes operation. This alarm cannot be auto-reset through 14-20.
checks: Check the safety circuit feeding terminals 37 and 38
Restore 24 V DC on both terminals
Apply a reset via fieldbus, digital input or the [Reset] key (if manual restart)
Review 5-19 for the STO reaction

fc280.name: Power card temperature
fc280.meaning: The power card cut-out temperature has exceeded its upper limit.
checks: Check the ambient temperature and cabinet ventilation
Check fans and filters; clean heatsink airways
Compare the heatsink temperature in 16-34

fc280.name: Drive initialized to default
fc280.meaning: All parameters have been set back to factory defaults.
checks: Re-enter motor data and application settings
Restore a saved LCP copy if available (0-50)

fc280.name: Auto DC braking
fc280.meaning: Occurs on IT mains when the drive coasts and the DC link exceeds 830 V (400 V units) or 425 V (200 V units); the motor is feeding energy into the DC link. This function can be switched in 0-07.
checks: Check the mains type setting in 0-06
Review 0-07 Auto DC Braking
Check for overhauling load during coast

fc280.name: Option detection
fc280.meaning: The option has been removed successfully.
checks: Confirm the removal is intended, then reset

fc280.name: Broken belt
fc280.meaning: A broken belt or coupling is suspected.
checks: Inspect the belt or coupling
Review broken-belt settings in 22-6*

fc280.name: Locked rotor
fc280.meaning: The rotor is blocked.
checks: Check for a mechanical jam
Review locked rotor detection settings 30-22 and 30-23

fc280.name: Position control fault
fc280.meaning: A fault occurred in position control.
checks: Check position feedback and the position control settings

fc280.name: Motor rotating
fc280.meaning: A PM motor is rotating while AMA is being performed.
checks: Stop the motor and make sure it is not being turned by the load before running AMA

fc280.name: Back EMF too high
fc280.meaning: The back EMF of the PM motor is too high before starting.
checks: Make sure the motor is not rotating before the start command
Check the back EMF setting (1-40)

fc280.name: STO internal fault
fc280.meaning: 24 V DC is applied to only one of the two STO terminals (37 and 38), or a fault was detected in the STO channels. Both terminals must be powered and the discrepancy between the two signals must be under 12 ms. This alarm cannot be auto-reset through 14-20.
checks: Check that both terminals 37 and 38 are powered from 24 V DC
Check the timing difference between the two channels
Contact the local Danfoss supplier if it persists

fc280.name: Not while running
fc280.meaning: Display message: the parameter can only be changed when the motor is stopped.
checks: Stop the motor, then change the parameter

fc280.name: Wrong password entered
fc280.meaning: Display message shown when a wrong password is used to change a password-protected parameter.
checks: Enter the correct main menu password (0-60)

mx2.name: Overcurrent at constant speed
mx2.meaning: Output current spiked to roughly twice the inverter rating while running at steady speed, so the output was cut.
checks: Look for sudden load changes and remove them
Check motor leads for short circuit between phases
Check motor and cable for an earth fault
Check the motor is not seized or locked
If a PM motor is used, confirm its parameters were set and tuned correctly

mx2.name: Overcurrent during deceleration
mx2.meaning: Output current spiked to roughly twice the inverter rating while slowing down.
checks: Lengthen the deceleration time
Check motor leads for a short circuit and the motor/cable for an earth fault
Check the motor is not jammed

mx2.name: Overcurrent during acceleration
mx2.meaning: Output current spiked to roughly twice the inverter rating while speeding up.
checks: Lengthen the acceleration time
Reduce the torque boost setting if it is high
Check the motor is not locked and the wiring is sound
For a PM motor verify motor data and tuning

mx2.name: Overcurrent in other conditions
mx2.meaning: Overcurrent trip outside the accel, decel and constant-speed cases.
checks: Reduce the DC injection braking power if it is set high
Check output wiring and the motor for a short circuit or earth fault
Check for a locked motor

mx2.name: Motor overload (electronic thermal)
mx2.meaning: The built-in electronic thermal model decided the motor was overloaded. With the separated thermal setting (b910) this is the motor protection. Reset is refused for about 10 s after the trip.
checks: Reduce the load
Check the electronic thermal level (b012/b212) matches the motor nameplate current
Lengthen the acceleration time if starting torque is marginal
Wait about 10 seconds before resetting

mx2.name: Braking resistor overload
mx2.meaning: Regenerative braking circuit usage went above the limit set in b090.
checks: Lengthen the deceleration time
Lengthen the duty cycle (fewer braking events per minute)
Check b090 and the braking resistor rating

mx2.name: Overvoltage (DC bus)
mx2.meaning: DC bus voltage rose above the trip level (about 400 V on 200 V class, 800 V on 400 V class) because of regeneration or high supply voltage.
checks: Lengthen the deceleration time
Check motor wiring/motor for an earth fault
Check whether the load drives the motor (overhauling) and reduce regeneration or add braking
Check the supply voltage; consider an AC reactor on the input

mx2.name: EEPROM error
mx2.meaning: Fault while accessing the internal EEPROM, often from noise or excessive temperature. Cannot be reset by RS terminal or STOP/RESET key; power cycle is required.
checks: Check for strong noise sources nearby and improve EMC measures
Check the heat sink is not clogged
Cycle power; if the error returns, initialise parameters (memory may be corrupt)

mx2.name: Undervoltage
mx2.meaning: DC bus voltage fell below the undervoltage level (about 173 V on 200 V class, 345 V on 400 V class).
checks: Check supply voltage
Check supply capacity is sufficient for the load/starting
Consider ageing of the DC bus capacitors

mx2.name: Current detector error
mx2.meaning: The inverter detected a fault in its current sensing circuit.
checks: Internal fault - the unit needs repair

mx2.name: CPU error
mx2.meaning: Malfunction or error in the internal CPU. Cannot be reset by RS terminal or STOP/RESET key; power cycle is required.
checks: Check for strong noise sources and improve EMC measures
If it persists after power cycling, the inverter is faulty - repair
If it persists, initialise parameters

mx2.name: External trip
mx2.meaning: A multi-function input programmed as EXT (12) turned ON.
checks: Check the external equipment wired to that input
Check wiring and the terminal contact logic (C011-C017)
Check for noise on the input wiring

mx2.name: USP error
mx2.meaning: Power was applied while a RUN command was already present, with the USP function enabled.
checks: Remove the RUN command before power-up
Check the RUN command wiring and source

mx2.name: Ground fault
mx2.meaning: An earth fault was detected between inverter output and motor at power-up. Cannot be reset by RS terminal or STOP/RESET key; power cycle is required.
checks: Check output wiring and motor insulation for an earth fault
Disconnect the motor leads and re-test to separate inverter from motor
Check the main circuit of the inverter (see maintenance section)

mx2.name: Input overvoltage
mx2.meaning: Supply voltage stayed high (DC bus about 390 V on 200 V class, 780 V on 400 V class) for 100 seconds.
checks: Lower the supply voltage / correct supply fluctuation
Install an AC reactor on the input

mx2.name: Temperature sensor error
mx2.meaning: The heat sink temperature sensing circuit reports an error such as a broken sensor line.
checks: Internal fault - the unit needs repair

mx2.name: Overtemperature
mx2.meaning: Main circuit temperature exceeded the allowed limit.
checks: Check the inverter is mounted vertically with proper clearances
Reduce ambient temperature
Check the cooling fan runs (set b092 to always on if needed) and its supply
Clean the heat sink fins

mx2.name: CPU communication error
mx2.meaning: Fault or malfunction in the internal CPU communication.
checks: Check for strong noise sources and improve EMC measures
If it persists, repair the inverter

mx2.name: Main circuit error
mx2.meaning: An error was detected on the main circuit board.
checks: Check for strong noise sources and improve EMC measures
If it persists, repair the inverter

mx2.name: Analog current input error
mx2.meaning: Excess current flowed into the FI analog current input terminal.
checks: Check FI wiring for a short circuit or wrong connection
If wiring is fine, the control board is faulty - repair

mx2.name: Driver error
mx2.meaning: The gate driver detected a momentary overcurrent (around 350% of rated), main-element overtemperature or driver supply drop. Cannot be reset by RS terminal or STOP/RESET key; power cycle is required.
checks: Check output wiring for a short circuit
Check motor and cables for an earth fault
Test the IGBT module for damage
Clean the heat sink fins

mx2.name: Thermistor error
mx2.meaning: The external thermistor input reads an abnormal motor temperature.
checks: Check the actual motor temperature
Check the thermistor and its wiring for damage
Separate thermistor wiring from noise sources
Check thermistor input settings (C005 = 19, C085)

mx2.name: Brake error
mx2.meaning: With brake control enabled (b120 = 01), the brake ON/OFF confirmation did not arrive within b124 after the release signal.
checks: Check the mechanical brake operates
Increase b124 if the time is too short
Check the brake confirmation input wiring (BOK)

mx2.name: Emergency shutoff (safety input)
mx2.meaning: The safety inputs GS1/GS2 were opened.
checks: Check GS1/GS2 wiring and the safety sequence
Check the GS input operation setting b145

mx2.name: Low-speed overload
mx2.meaning: The electronic thermal function detected an overload at extremely low speed (0.2 Hz or less); with the separated setting (b910) this is the inverter protection. The history may show a higher frequency.
checks: Reduce the load, particularly at very low speed
Check electronic thermal settings (b012, b910)

mx2.name: Digital Operator connection error
mx2.meaning: Communication with the remote operator 3G3AX-OP01 failed or the cable was disconnected (detection can be disabled with b165 = 02).
checks: Check or replace the operator cable
Review b165

mx2.name: Modbus communication error
mx2.meaning: A communication timeout occurred while C076 is set to trip.
checks: Check communication speed and settings match the master
Check wire length and cable quality
Check for a broken wire
Check the terminating resistor setting

mx2.name: DriveProgramming program error
mx2.meaning: Errors raised by the built-in DriveProgramming function (program faults).
checks: See the separate DriveProgramming manual for the cause of the specific code

mx2.name: DriveProgramming user trip
mx2.meaning: User-defined trips generated by a DriveProgramming program.
checks: See the DriveProgramming manual and the user program for the trip meaning

mx2.name: Option unit error
mx2.meaning: Error reported by an installed option unit (for example the EtherCAT unit).
checks: See the manual for the option unit installed

mx2.name: Option communication timeout
mx2.meaning: Communication between the inverter and the option unit timed out.
checks: Check the option unit is seated correctly and its fixing screws are tight
If properly mounted, the option unit may be faulty

mx2.name: Encoder disconnection
mx2.meaning: Measured motor speed stayed below the starting frequency (b082) for the P077 time while output was at or above creep speed P015; the real frequency monitor d008 is set to 0.
checks: Check encoder wiring for a break or wrong connection
Slightly raise P077 and P015

mx2.name: Overspeed
mx2.meaning: Motor speed from the encoder exceeded the P026 level (P026 not zero); d008 is set to 0.
checks: Check encoder wiring
Check the encoder pulse count setting (P011)
Check the load conditions and frequency setting F001
Adjust the overspeed level P026

mx2.name: Position control range trip
mx2.meaning: During simple position control the current position went outside the limits P072/P073.
checks: Check the current position and the limits P072/P073
Check position commands P060-P067
Check the origin

mx2.name: STO self-diagnosis error
mx2.meaning: A fault was found in the STO input terminals or internal safety circuit; independent of the b145 setting.
checks: Perform the periodic functional test of the safety function
Check for strong noise sources
Internal safety circuit may be faulty - repair

mx2.name: Parameter conflict warning
mx2.meaning: When one setting contradicts another (for example a frequency limit above the maximum frequency, or a start frequency above a limit) the PRG LED blinks and the RUN command is ignored. The latest warning code is stored in d090.
checks: Read d090 to see which parameter pair conflicts
Correct the settings: frequency upper/lower limits (A061/A062) vs maximum frequency (A004), start frequency (b082) vs limits and jogging, set frequency vs jump frequencies

pf520.name: Auxiliary input
pf520.meaning: An external trip signal wired to a digital input set as Aux Fault has opened, so the drive stopped on purpose.
checks: Check the remote/external trip wiring and the device feeding that input
If the fault is not expected, review the digital input programming (t062, t063, t065-t068 set to 12 Aux Fault) and any comms-driven trip

pf520.name: Power loss
pf520.meaning: The drive saw a single-phase supply condition while carrying a heavy load.
checks: Look for low voltage or interruptions on the incoming AC supply
Check the input fuses
Reduce the load

pf520.name: Undervoltage
pf520.meaning: The DC bus fell below its minimum level, usually because the supply sagged or dropped out.
checks: Monitor the incoming AC line for low voltage or short interruptions

pf520.name: Overvoltage
pf520.meaning: The DC bus rose above its maximum level, from a high supply, line transients or motor regeneration.
checks: Monitor the AC line for high voltage or transients
If the motor regenerates, lengthen the decel time or fit a dynamic brake resistor option

pf520.name: Motor stalled
pf520.meaning: The drive could not accelerate or decelerate the motor, typically because it sat in current limit too long.
checks: Increase accel time (P041, A442, A444, A446) or reduce the load so output current stays below the current limit (A484, A485)
Check for an overhauling load

pf520.name: Motor overload
pf520.meaning: The internal electronic overload protection tripped because the motor drew excessive current for too long.
checks: Reduce the load so output current stays below the motor overload current (P033)
Verify the boost setting A530

pf520.name: Heatsink overtemperature
pf520.meaning: The heatsink/power module temperature exceeded its limit.
checks: Check for blocked or dirty heatsink fins and confirm ambient temperature is within rating
Check the cooling fan

pf520.name: Control module overtemperature
pf520.meaning: The control module temperature exceeded its limit.
checks: Check ambient temperature
Check for airflow obstruction
Check for dirt or debris
Check the fan

pf520.name: Hardware overcurrent
pf520.meaning: Drive output current exceeded the hardware current limit.
checks: Check programming
Check for excess load, wrong boost setting (A530), or DC brake voltage set too high, and other causes of excess current

pf520.name: Ground fault
pf520.meaning: A current path to earth was detected at one or more drive output terminals.
checks: Check the motor and external wiring from the output terminals for a grounded condition

pf520.name: Load loss
pf520.meaning: Output torque current stayed below the A490 level for longer than A491 time, so the load appears to be lost (e.g. broken belt or coupling).
checks: Verify the connection between motor and load
Verify the level (A490) and time (A491) settings

pf520.name: Output phase loss
pf520.meaning: Loss of an output phase was detected (only when the function is enabled with A557).
checks: Verify the motor wiring
Verify the motor

pf520.name: Analog input loss
pf520.meaning: An analog input configured to fault on signal loss has lost its signal.
checks: Check for broken or loose connections at the inputs
Check parameters t094 / t097 (signal-loss action)

pf520.name: Auto restart tries exceeded
pf520.meaning: The drive tried to reset a fault and resume running the number of times set in A541 and did not succeed.
checks: Correct the cause of the underlying fault and clear it manually

pf520.name: Phase U to ground
pf520.meaning: A ground fault was detected on motor phase U between the drive and the motor.
checks: Check the wiring between drive and motor
Check the motor for a grounded phase
Replace the drive if the fault cannot be cleared

pf520.name: Phase V to ground
pf520.meaning: A ground fault was detected on motor phase V between the drive and the motor.
checks: Check the wiring between drive and motor
Check the motor for a grounded phase
Replace the drive if the fault cannot be cleared

pf520.name: Phase W to ground
pf520.meaning: A ground fault was detected on motor phase W between the drive and the motor.
checks: Check the wiring between drive and motor
Check the motor for a grounded phase
Replace the drive if the fault cannot be cleared

pf520.name: Phase UV short
pf520.meaning: Excessive current was detected between two output terminals (UV), indicating a short.
checks: Check the motor and drive output terminal wiring for a short
Replace the drive if the fault cannot be cleared

pf520.name: Phase UW short
pf520.meaning: Excessive current was detected between two output terminals (UW), indicating a short.
checks: Check the motor and drive output terminal wiring for a short
Replace the drive if the fault cannot be cleared

pf520.name: Phase VW short
pf520.meaning: Excessive current was detected between two output terminals (VW), indicating a short.
checks: Check the motor and drive output terminal wiring for a short
Replace the drive if the fault cannot be cleared

pf520.name: Parameters defaulted
pf520.meaning: The drive was told to write factory default values to EEPROM.
checks: Clear the fault or cycle power
Re-program the drive parameters as needed

pf520.name: Safety open
pf520.meaning: Both safety inputs (Safety 1 and Safety 2) are de-energised, and t105 is set to fault in that state.
checks: Check the safety input signals
If safety is not used, verify and tighten the jumper across terminals S1, S2 and S+

pf520.name: Software overcurrent (shear pin)
pf520.meaning: Current stayed above the shear pin level (A486/A488) for longer than the shear pin time (A487/A489).
checks: Verify the connection between motor and load
Verify the level and time settings

pf520.name: Drive overload
pf520.meaning: The drive's own overload rating was exceeded.
checks: Reduce the load or extend the accel time

pf520.name: Power unit
pf520.meaning: A failure was detected in the drive power section.
checks: Check that the maximum ambient temperature has not been exceeded
Cycle power
Replace the drive if the fault cannot be cleared

pf520.name: DSI network loss
pf520.meaning: Control over the Modbus/DSI (RS-485) link was interrupted.
checks: Cycle power
Check the communications cabling
Check the Modbus/DSI settings and status

pf520.name: Option card network loss
pf520.meaning: Control through the remote network of the optional network card was interrupted.
checks: Cycle power
Check the communications cabling
Check the network adapter settings
Check the external network status

pf520.name: Embedded EtherNet/IP network loss
pf520.meaning: Control through the embedded EtherNet/IP adapter was interrupted.
checks: Cycle power
Check the communications cabling
Check the EtherNet/IP settings
Check the external network status

pf520.name: Autotune failure
pf520.meaning: The autotune routine was cancelled by the user or did not complete successfully.
checks: Restart the procedure
Cycle power

pf520.name: DSI communication loss
pf520.meaning: Communication between the drive and the Modbus/DSI master was interrupted.
checks: Cycle power
Check the communications cabling
Check the Modbus/DSI settings and status
Modify the response with C125 (Comm Loss Action)
Connecting I/O terminals C1 and C2 to ground may improve noise immunity
Replace the wiring, Modbus master device or control module

pf520.name: Option card communication loss
pf520.meaning: Communication between the drive and the network option card was interrupted.
checks: Cycle power
Reinstall the option card in the drive
Modify the response with C125 (Comm Loss Action)
Replace the wiring, port expander, option card or control module

pf520.name: Embedded EtherNet/IP communication loss
pf520.meaning: Internal communication between the drive and the embedded EtherNet/IP adapter was interrupted.
checks: Cycle power
Check the EtherNet/IP settings
Check the drive's Ethernet settings and diagnostic parameters
Modify the response with C125 (Comm Loss Action)
Replace the wiring, Ethernet switch or control module

pf520.name: Encoder loss
pf520.meaning: One of the two encoder channel signals is missing (differential encoder required).
checks: Check the wiring
If P047/P049/P051 = 16 Positioning and A535 = 5 Quad Check, swap the encoder channel inputs or any two motor leads
Replace the encoder

pf520.name: Function loss
pf520.meaning: The Freeze-Fire (Function Loss) input is inactive, i.e. the input to the programmed terminal is open.
checks: Close the input to the terminal and cycle power

pf520.name: Parameter checksum error
pf520.meaning: The drive's non-volatile parameter storage is corrupted.
checks: Set P053 (Reset To Defaults) to 2 Factory Rset

pf520.name: External storage error
pf520.meaning: External non-volatile storage has failed.
checks: Set P053 (Reset To Defaults) to 2 Factory Rset

pf520.name: Control module connect error
pf520.meaning: The control module was disconnected while the drive was powered.
checks: Clear the fault and verify all parameter settings
Never remove or install the control module with power applied

pf520.name: Incompatible control/power module
pf520.meaning: The PowerFlex 525 control module does not support a power module with 0.25 HP rating.
checks: Change to a different power module
Change to a PowerFlex 523 control module

pf520.name: Replaced control/power module
pf520.meaning: The control module could not recognise the power module (hardware failure).
checks: Change to a different power module
Replace the control module if changing the power module does not help

pf520.name: Control/power module mismatch
pf520.meaning: The control module was mounted on a different drive type of power module.
checks: Set P053 (Reset To Defaults) to 3 Power Reset

pf520.name: Keypad membrane
pf520.meaning: The keypad membrane has failed or is disconnected.
checks: Cycle power
Replace the control module if the fault cannot be cleared

pf520.name: Safety hardware
pf520.meaning: A malfunction in the safety input enable hardware; one of the safety inputs is not enabled.
checks: Cycle power
Check the safety input signals; if safety is not used, verify and tighten the jumper across terminals S1, S2 and S+
Verify the safety hardware; replace the control module if the fault cannot be cleared

pf520.name: Microprocessor failure
pf520.meaning: Microprocessor failure.
checks: Cycle power
Verify grounding requirements (see General Grounding Requirements in the manual)
Replace the control module if the fault cannot be cleared

pf520.name: I/O board failure
pf520.meaning: A failure was detected in the drive control and I/O section.
checks: Cycle power
Replace the drive or control module if the fault cannot be cleared

pf520.name: Flash update required
pf520.meaning: The drive firmware is corrupt, mismatched or incompatible with the hardware.
checks: Perform a firmware flash update to load a valid set of firmware

pf520.name: Non-recoverable error
pf520.meaning: A non-recoverable firmware or hardware error was detected; the drive stopped and reset itself.
checks: Clear the fault or cycle power
Replace the drive or control module if the fault cannot be cleared

pf520.name: DSI flash update required
pf520.meaning: A critical firmware problem was detected and the drive is running backup firmware that supports only DSI communications.
checks: Perform a firmware flash update over DSI communications to load a valid set of firmware

wj200.name: Over-current at constant speed
wj200.meaning: Output current went above the safe limit while the drive was running at steady speed (short circuit, locked rotor or heavy load). Output is switched off.
checks: Look for a shorted motor lead or phase-to-phase / phase-to-earth fault: disconnect the motor and megger the cable and motor windings
Check that the motor shaft turns freely and the load is not jammed or overloaded
On a dual-voltage motor, confirm the star/delta link arrangement matches the supply voltage

wj200.name: Over-current during deceleration
wj200.meaning: Excess output current was detected while slowing down; output is cut. The manual gives the same cause hints as E01.
checks: Look for a shorted motor lead or phase-to-phase / phase-to-earth fault: disconnect the motor and megger the cable and motor windings
Check that the motor shaft turns freely and the load is not jammed or overloaded
On a dual-voltage motor, confirm the star/delta link arrangement matches the supply voltage
Lengthen the deceleration time (F003 / A093) if the load inertia is high

wj200.name: Over-current during acceleration
wj200.meaning: Excess output current was detected while speeding up; output is cut. Same cause hints as E01.
checks: Look for a shorted motor lead or phase-to-phase / phase-to-earth fault: disconnect the motor and megger the cable and motor windings
Check that the motor shaft turns freely and the load is not jammed or overloaded
On a dual-voltage motor, confirm the star/delta link arrangement matches the supply voltage
Lengthen the acceleration time (F002 / A092) or review torque boost (A042) and V/f settings

wj200.name: Over-current in other conditions
wj200.meaning: Over-current occurred at a time that is not constant speed, acceleration or deceleration. Same cause hints as E01.
checks: Look for a shorted motor lead or phase-to-phase / phase-to-earth fault: disconnect the motor and megger the cable and motor windings
Check that the motor shaft turns freely and the load is not jammed or overloaded
On a dual-voltage motor, confirm the star/delta link arrangement matches the supply voltage

wj200.name: Motor overload (electronic thermal)
wj200.meaning: The drive's electronic thermal model decided the motor was overloaded and tripped the output.
checks: Check mechanical load and look for binding or a blocked fan/process
Verify the thermal level b012 matches the motor nameplate current and the characteristic b013 suits the motor
Check motor capacity H003 and pole count H004 are entered correctly

wj200.name: Braking resistor overload
wj200.meaning: The braking-chopper duty ratio went above the limit set in b090, so the drive shut off its output.
checks: Check b090 against the resistor's rating
Reduce regeneration: lengthen the deceleration time or use a larger / additional braking resistor
Check b097 resistor value setting is correct

wj200.name: Over-voltage
wj200.meaning: The DC bus voltage rose above its limit, for example from regenerative energy from the motor or a high supply voltage.
checks: Lengthen the deceleration time or enable deceleration over-voltage suppression (b130)
Fit or check a braking resistor / unit for overhauling loads
Measure the incoming supply voltage for surges or an over-high level

wj200.name: EEPROM error
wj200.meaning: The built-in memory had a problem, typically due to noise or high temperature, and the output was shut off.
checks: Cycle power; resets from RS terminal or STOP/RESET are not accepted for this trip
If it repeats, initialise the drive (b084 / b180) and re-enter settings
Review earthing, cable routing and cabinet temperature for noise/heat

wj200.name: Under-voltage
wj200.meaning: The internal DC bus voltage dropped under its threshold, which can cause control faults, motor heating or weak torque. The drive shuts off its output.
checks: Measure the supply voltage on all phases and look for dips or a missing phase
Check input contactor, fuses, terminals and any input reactor
See restart-after-undervoltage settings b001 to b005

wj200.name: Current detection error
wj200.meaning: A fault in the drive's internal current sensing circuit was detected and the output was shut off.
checks: Cycle power and retry
Check for heavy noise sources or earthing problems
If it persists the drive likely needs repair

wj200.name: CPU error
wj200.meaning: The drive's processor malfunctioned and the output was switched off.
checks: Cycle power and retry
Check earthing and noise suppression
If it repeats, have the drive repaired or replaced

wj200.name: External trip
wj200.meaning: A digital input assigned to the EXT function (option 12) was activated, so the drive latched a trip.
checks: Find which input is set to EXT in C001-C007 and check what is wired to it
Check the external device or interlock contact that triggered it
Check input logic (C011-C017) in case of an NO/NC mismatch

wj200.name: Unattended start protection (USP)
wj200.meaning: Power was applied while a run command was already active and USP was enabled, so the drive refused to start.
checks: Remove the run command (FW/RV) and then reset, or press reset
Wait at least 3 seconds after power-up before giving a run command
Disable the USP input if automatic start on power-up is wanted

wj200.name: Ground fault
wj200.meaning: A ground fault between the drive output and the motor was found during the power-up test. This protects the drive, not people.
checks: Disconnect the motor and insulation-test the motor and cable to earth
Check for moisture or damaged cable insulation
Reset is not accepted; cycle power, and initialise if the fault persists

wj200.name: Input over-voltage
wj200.meaning: The drive checks incoming voltage after 100 seconds in stop mode and tripped because the level was too high.
checks: Measure the supply voltage and compare with the drive's rating
Check for surges from other equipment or power factor correction caps
After clearing, the drive can run again

wj200.name: Inverter thermal sensor error
wj200.meaning: The thermal sensor inside the power module is not connected / not being read.
checks: Cycle power and retry
If persistent the drive hardware needs repair

wj200.name: Inverter over-temperature
wj200.meaning: The temperature of the power devices went above the allowed level, so the drive tripped.
checks: Check the cooling fan runs and the heatsink and vents are clean
Check cabinet and ambient temperature (b075) and clearances
Reduce load or carrier frequency (b083); check automatic carrier reduction b089

wj200.name: CPU communication error
wj200.meaning: Communication between the drive's two processors failed.
checks: Cycle power and retry
Check earthing and noise
Repair or replace if it recurs

wj200.name: Main circuit error
wj200.meaning: The drive could not confirm that its main power supply circuit was established, because of noise or a damaged main-circuit part.
checks: Cycle power; check the main power connection and fuses
Check for noise sources and earthing
Repair if it persists

wj200.name: Driver error
wj200.meaning: A fault in the safety protection circuit between the CPU and the output driver was detected, possibly from heavy electrical noise. The output stage was turned off.
checks: Reset by key/terminal is not accepted; cycle power
Improve earthing, shielding and cable separation to reduce noise
Initialise the drive if it recurs, then repair if still present

wj200.name: Thermistor trip
wj200.meaning: The motor thermistor connected to terminals 5 and L indicated an over-temperature, so the output was turned off.
checks: Check the motor temperature, ventilation and load
Check the thermistor wiring and the PTC function setting on terminal 5 (C005 = 19)
Check the thermistor calibration C085

wj200.name: Brake error
wj200.meaning: With brake control enabled (b120 = 01) the drive did not receive the brake confirmation signal within the confirmation wait time b124 after sending brake release.
checks: Check the brake confirmation (BOK) input wiring and the brake itself
Check b121-b127 timing and release settings
Check the brake actually lifts

wj200.name: Safe stop
wj200.meaning: The safe-stop (GS) input was triggered when b145 is set to 01.
checks: Check the safety circuit wired to GS1 and GS2 and the emergency stop device
The STOP/RESET key cannot reset it; cycle power
Initialise if the same trip returns

wj200.name: Low-speed overload
wj200.meaning: The drive detected an overload while running at very low speed and shut off the output.
checks: Check the load and motor at low speed for binding
Check the motor cooling at low speed
Review overload settings (b012, b021-b023)

wj200.name: Operator connection error
wj200.meaning: Communication between the drive and its keypad/operator failed.
checks: Check the operator cable and connector seating
Check the keypad for damage
See external operator loss action b165

wj200.name: Modbus communication error
wj200.meaning: A Modbus timeout occurred while the communication error action was set to trip (C076 = 00).
checks: Check the RS-485 wiring, termination and polarity
Check master polling interval against timeout C077
Check C071-C075 communication settings and C072 address match the master

wj200.name: EzSQ invalid instruction
wj200.meaning: The stored EzSQ program is corrupt, or the PRG input was turned on when no program was downloaded.
checks: Re-download the EzSQ program
Check the PRG terminal function and A017 setting if no program is used

wj200.name: EzSQ nesting count error
wj200.meaning: In the EzSQ program, subroutines, if-statements or for-next loops are nested deeper than eight levels.
checks: Simplify the program structure to eight levels or fewer and re-download

wj200.name: EzSQ instruction error
wj200.meaning: The drive met a program instruction it cannot execute.
checks: Review the EzSQ program for unsupported or invalid instructions and re-download

wj200.name: EzSQ user trip 0 to 9
wj200.meaning: User-defined trips raised by the EzSQ program (E50 to E59 correspond to user trip 0 to 9).
checks: Check the EzSQ program source to see which condition raises the trip

wj200.name: Option board error
wj200.meaning: The drive detected an error in the option board fitted in the option slot.
checks: Reseat the option board and check it is compatible
See the option board's instruction manual for the specific code
Check P001 for the action on option errors

wj200.name: Encoder disconnection
wj200.meaning: An encoder connection error was found: broken wiring, failed encoder, or an encoder that does not support line driver output.
checks: Check encoder wiring and shield
Check the encoder type and supply
Check P003, P004 and P011 settings

wj200.name: Excessive speed
wj200.meaning: Motor speed reached or exceeded the maximum frequency (A004) multiplied by the over-speed detection level (P026).
checks: Check encoder feedback and settings
Review A004 and P026
Check for an overhauling load

wj200.name: Positioning range error
wj200.meaning: The current position went outside the allowed position range set by P072 and P073.
checks: Review P072/P073 limits and the positioning set-up

wj200.name: Outside failure (safe stop)
wj200.meaning: Raised from the safe stop signal when b145 = 02 (outside failure).
checks: Check GS1, GS2 and EDM wiring and the external safety device
Reset by terminal/key is not accepted; cycle power

wj200.name: Inside failure (safe stop)
wj200.meaning: Raised from the safe stop signal when b145 = 02, 03 or 05 (inside failure).
checks: Check GS1, GS2 and EDM wiring and the external safety device
Reset by terminal/key is not accepted; cycle power
